body:
As you can see in the [design](https://app.zeplin.io/project/5acc8becfc0c980068fc12cc/screen/5cd1a7992e4f02039b5a8336), the `rangeInput` is wrapped in the same panel as `rangeSlider`. However, InstantSearch.js only supports wrapping a single widget in a panel.

This will be required once the styles come.
I'm not sure if this pattern is really necessary in an example like this
What would you have used? It's to import them all from `widgets/index.js`.

since all widgets are always mounted, I would've gone for the regular way of calling the functions inline in the main file. I understand why you split it up here, but I fear like it might confuse people

The goal of the demo is also to educate people how to build apps with InstantSearch. I tried several patterns and this once seem like an easy structure to work with. It will be easy to migrate this demo to React/Vue/etc. 

We've often neglected how to integrate InstantSearch into apps and most of our examples don't make usage of modern JavaScript features that we usually like working with.
seems like most of these aren't necessary here
